nodes.name: Thermal decomposition CuNiNP synthesis
nodes.procedure: Before synthesis, all glassware was cleaned with aqua regia, thoroughly rinsed with distilled water, and dried overnight at 130°C. For Cu50Ni50NP, 1.9·10^-3 mol of copper acetylacetonate, 1.9·10^-3 mol of nickel acetylacetonate, and 6 ml of OAm were added to a 250 ml round flask. The color changed from pale violet (for copper acetylacetonate) and pale green (for nickel acetylacetonate) to blue turquoise, suggesting a modification in the coordination structure of the metal cations. After adding 10 ml of TOP, the flask was connected to a nitrogen inlet and a condenser. The solution was vigorously stirred for 30 minutes at 70°C under an inert atmosphere, forming a homogeneous blue-turquoise solution (molar ratio metal precursor:OAm:TOP = 1:4.7:5.7). The round flask was transferred to a second bath pre-heated at 250°C with continuous stirring at 750 rpm. After 1 minute, the solution turned black indicating thermal decomposition and nanoparticle formation. Reaction continued for 30 min, then cooled naturally to room temperature. Nanoparticles were recovered by adding 120 ml hexane/ethanol (30:70% v/v), centrifuged at 9000 rpm for 10 min, re-dispersed in hexane/ethanol by sonication, and purified 3 times. Final product stored under inert atmosphere in glovebox. Other compositions (Cu75Ni25NP, Cu25Ni75NP, NiNP) used same protocol with different metal precursor ratios.
